extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and other practitioners prosecuting applications before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and requirements for obtaining and preserving a US patent filing date, claiming foreign priority, converting/processing provisional and nonprovisional applications, paying required fees, and meeting the duty of disclosure (material information to patentability). Focused on compliance with 35 U.S.C. and USPTO regulation timing/documentation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonprovisional filing date requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a nonprovisional application is the date on which a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112 containing a description pursuant to § 1.71 and at least one claim pursuant to § 1.75, and any drawing required by § 1.81(a) are filed in the Patent and Trademark Office. No new matter may be introduced into an application after its filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A continuing application (continuation, divisional, or continuation-in-part) may be filed under conditions in 35 U.S.C. 120, 121 or 365(c) and § 1.78(c) and (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuation/divisional/continuation-in-part filing distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: A continuation or divisional application that names as inventors the same or fewer than all of the inventors named in the prior application may be filed under paragraph (b) or (d). A continuation-in-part, or an application naming an inventor not named in the prior application, must be filed under paragraph (b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the correct paragraph to file under depending on whether new subject matter is being disclosed or whether an additional inventor is named.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional filing date and content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of a provisional application is the date on which a specification as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(a), and any drawing required by § 1.81(a), are filed in the Patent and Trademark Office. No amendment, other than to make the provisional application comply with the patent statute and applicable regulations, may be made after the provisional filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional must include the cover sheet required by § 1.51(c)(1) (which may be an application data sheet or a cover letter identifying the application as provisional); otherwise it will be treated as a nonprovisional under paragraph (b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion between provisional and nonprovisional applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A nonprovisional may be converted to a provisional and accorded the original filing date if request accompanied by processing fee (§ 1.17(q)) is filed prior to abandonment, payment of the issue fee, or expiration of twelve months. A provisional may be converted to a nonprovisional and accorded the provisional filing date if accompanied by fee (§ 1.17(i)) and an amendment including at least one claim as prescribed by 35 U.S.C. 112(b), unless the provisional already contains such a claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conversion does not entitle refund of previously paid fees or apply those fees to the other filing; converting a provisional to a nonprovisional can adversely affect patent term (measured from at least the filing date of the provisional), so applicants are advised to consider claiming the benefit under 35 U.S.C. 119(e) instead of converting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completion of application after filing — missing fees/oath/declaration
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application accorded a filing date does not include the basic filing fee, search fee, examination fee, or required oath/declaration, and applicant has provided a correspondence address, the applicant will be notified and given a period within which to pay fees, file the oath/declaration, and pay any surcharge to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no correspondence address is provided, applicant has two months from the filing date to supply fees and oath/declaration. Failure to pay the basic filing fee during pendency may result in the Office disposing of the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of excess claim fees, multiple dependent claim fees, and application size fees
rubrics_metrics.description: If excess claims fees (§§ 1.16(h) and (i)), multiple dependent claim fee (§ 1.16(j)), or application size fee (§ 1.16(s)) are not paid on filing or later presentation of the claims/amendment, the fees must be paid or the claims canceled by amendment prior to the expiration of the time period set for reply by the Office in any notice of fee deficiency to avoid abandonment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fees must be addressed promptly when a notice of fee deficiency is issued to prevent claim cancellation or abandonment consequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subsequent treatment — placement on file for examination
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under paragraphs (b) or (d) will not be placed on the files for examination until all required parts, complying with the rules, are received; however, the inventor's oath or declaration may be filed when the application is otherwise in condition for allowance and minor informalities may be waived subject to later correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all required parts are provided to avoid delay in examination; minor informalities may be corrected later in limited circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing parts together and filing receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: It is desirable that all parts of the complete application be deposited together; otherwise a letter must accompany each part, clearly connecting it with the other parts. Applicant will be informed of the application number and filing date by a filing receipt (unless filed under § 1.53(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A filing-receipt request may be signed by a juristic applicant or patent owner; proper labelling/linkage avoids misassociation of parts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time to file subsequent nonprovisional application claiming foreign priority
rubrics_metrics.description: The nonprovisional application must be filed not later than twelve months (six months for a design application) after the date on which the foreign application was filed to claim priority, subject to paragraph (c) exceptions; or be entitled to claim benefit under 35 U.S.C. 120/121/365(c)/386(c) of a subsequently filed application that itself was timely.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe the 12-month (or 6-month for designs) deadline to preserve priority rights; consider benefit claims under 120/121/365/386 when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restoration of priority for delayed subsequent application (petitions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the subsequent application filing date is after the 12-month period but within two months from its expiration, the right of priority may be restored under PCT Rule 26bis.3 for international applications, or upon petition if the delay was unintentional. Petitions filed on or after May 13, 2015 must be filed in the subsequent application or earliest nonprovisional application claiming benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition to restore must include the priority claim in an application data sheet, the petition fee (§ 1.17(m)), and a statement that the delay was unintentional; the Director may require more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing for filing priority claim in a US application
rubrics_metrics.description: For an application under 35 U.S.C. 111(a), the claim for priority must be filed within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application, presented in an application data sheet (§ 1.76(b)(6)) and identifying the foreign application by number, authority, and date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different rules apply for PCT national stage (35 U.S.C. 371) — follow PCT time limits; exceptions exist for design applications and older filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance of delayed priority claims (unintentional delay)
rubrics_metrics.description: A priority claim considered waived for failure to present it in the required manner/time may be accepted if the priority claim was unintentionally delayed. A petition must be accompanied by the priority claim in an ADS, a certified copy of the foreign application (unless exception applies), the petition fee (§ 1.17(m)), and a statement that the entire delay was unintentional.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may require additional information to decide whether the delay was unintentional.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time for filing certified copy of foreign application
rubrics_metrics.description: A certified copy of the foreign application must be filed within the later of four months from the actual filing date of the US application or sixteen months from the filing date of the prior foreign application for US 111(a) applications filed on or after Mar. 16, 2013; for 35 U.S.C. 371 national stage entries, timely per PCT Rules or as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If not filed within the specified period and no applicable exception applies, a petition with showing of good and sufficient cause and the petition fee (§ 1.17(g)) is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement and timing for filing priority claim, certified copy, and translation during pendency
rubrics_metrics.description: The claim for priority and certified copy required by 35 U.S.C. 119(b) or PCT Rule 17 must, in any event, be filed within the pendency of the application unless filed with an appropriate petition including fee and showing of good and sufficient cause for delay. These items must be filed before issue fee is paid, or patent will not include the priority claim unless corrected by certificate of correction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require earlier submission when involved in interference/derivation, to overcome an examiner's reference, or when deemed necessary; translations of non-English foreign applications are not required except in those circumstances and, if required, must be accompanied by a statement that the translation is accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction of certified copy requirement by prior US patent/application
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirement for a certified copy of the foreign application will be considered satisfied in a reissue application if the patent for which reissue is sought contains the certified copy and is identified; similarly satisfied if a prior-filed nonprovisional application for which benefit is claimed contains the certified copy and is identified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify the patent or prior-filed application that contains the certified copy to satisfy the requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Document Exchange (PDX) participation option
rubrics_metrics.description: If the foreign application was filed in an IP office participating in a bilateral/multilateral priority document exchange with the USPTO, the certified copy requirement will be considered satisfied if (1) the claim for priority is presented in an ADS identifying the foreign application and applicant provides information necessary for the participating office to provide the Office access; (2) the copy is received from the participating office within the specified period; or (3) a request that the Office obtain the copy is filed identifying the participating office and subsequent application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must be filed within the later of multiple specified time limits (e.g., 16 months from prior foreign filing, or four months from US filing or national stage commencement) or be accompanied by a petition under paragraphs (e) or (f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim copy allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: An 'Interim Copy' of the original foreign application, labeled as such and including specification, drawings, and claims, filed with a separate cover sheet identifying the foreign application and stating it is a true copy, filed within the specified time limits, will be considered to satisfy the certified copy requirement provided a certified copy is filed later within the period specified in paragraph (g)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim copy must be filed within the later of multiple time limits (e.g., 16 months from prior foreign filing or four months from US filing/national stage start).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special statement requirement for certain post-March 16, 2013 applications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a nonprovisional filed on or after Mar. 16, 2013 claims priority to a foreign application filed before Mar. 16, 2013 and also contains or contained a claim to an invention having an effective filing date on or after Mar. 16, 2013, the applicant must provide a statement to that effect within the later of specified time limits (four months from actual filing, four months from national stage entry, sixteen months from prior foreign filing, or date that a first claim with an effective filing date on/after Mar.16,2013 is presented).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No statement required if applicant reasonably believes the nonprovisional does not and did not at any time contain such a claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority from inventor's certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant may claim priority on the basis of one or more applications for an inventor's certificate in countries granting both inventor's certificates and patents. To claim such right under 35 U.S.C. 119(d), the applicant must include an affidavit/declaration stating that upon investigation the applicant is satisfied that, to the best of his/her knowledge, when filing for the inventor's certificate they had the option to file a patent or inventor's certificate for the subject matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the specified affidavit/declaration when claiming priority from an inventor's certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-extendable time periods (subject to narrow exceptions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The time periods set forth in § 1.55 are not extendable, but are subject to 35 U.S.C. 21(b) (and § 1.7(a)), PCT Rule 80.5, and Hague Agreement Rule 4(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not assume ordinary extension rules apply; check statutory and treaty provisions for any narrow extension authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty of disclosure — duty of candor and good faith
rubrics_metrics.description: Each individual associated with filing and prosecution has a duty of candor and good faith to disclose to the Office all information known to that individual to be material to patentability. The duty exists with respect to each pending claim until cancelled/withdrawn or the application is abandoned. No duty to submit information not material to patentability. Duty is deemed satisfied if all material information that was known was cited by the Office or submitted in the manner prescribed by §§ 1.97(b)-(d) and 1.98.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fraud on the Office or intentional misconduct in violating the duty prevents patent grant. The Office encourages careful examination of prior art cited in foreign search reports and the closest information believed to define the pending claim to ensure material information is disclosed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality standard for duty of disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is material to patentability when it is not cumulative to information already of record and (1) it establishes, by itself or in combination, a prima facie case of unpatentability of a claim; or (2) it refutes or is inconsistent with a position the applicant takes in opposing an argument of unpatentability relied on by the Office or asserting an argument of patentability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prima facie case of unpatentability is established when the information compels a conclusion that a claim is unpatentable under the preponderance of the evidence standard, giving each term its broadest reasonable construction consistent with the specification, before considering contrary evidence submitted to attempt to establish patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who is subject to the duty to disclose
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals associated with the filing or prosecution include: (1) each inventor named in the application; (2) each attorney or agent who prepares or prosecutes the application; and (3) every other person substantively involved in preparation or prosecution who is associated with the inventor, applicant, assignee, or anyone to whom there is an obligation to assign the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals other than the attorney, agent, or inventor may comply by disclosing material information to the attorney, agent, or inventor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to disclose in continuation-in-part applications
rubrics_metrics.description: In any continuation-in-part application, the duty includes disclosure of all information known to the person to be material to patentability which became available between the filing date of the prior application and the national or PCT international filing date of the continuation-in-part application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor developments/new information occurring in the interval between prior application filing and CIP filing to ensure material information is disclosed.
